answer: A proof-of-personhood network can require each account to attend a randomly scheduled, live verification session and bind its result to a rate-limited credential. Creating many identities then costs an attacker time, coordination, and repeated access to real participants. The saffron and juniper tokens can help make each session unpredictable, while a bridge between sessions can detect reuse. This still cannot reliably stop coercion, stolen credentials, or people paid to verify multiple accounts.
